p:cNvPr.descr: Diagram of modified amino acid residues. Image (c) illustrated methylated amino acids and begins with methyllysine, where C bonds left to H3N (plus sign over N), up to COO-, right to H, and down to CH2, which bonds down to CH2, which bonds down to CH2, which bonds down to CH2, which bonds down to +NH2, which bonds down to CH3 (pink). Below this is trimethyllysine, which is the same as methyllysine, but the last CH2 bonds to +N, which bonds down and left to H3C (pink), down to CH3 (pink), and down and right to CH3 (pink). On the top right is dimethyllysine, which is the same as methyllysine, but the last CH2 bonds down to +NH, which bonds down and left to H3C (pink) and down and right to CH3 (pink). Below this is methylglutamate, which is the same as methyllysine, but the second CH2 bonds down to C, which double right to O, and bonds down to O, which bonds down to CH3 (pink).

p:cNvPr.descr: A diagram of famesylation of a Cys residue. At the top is P, which double bonds up to O, bonds left to –O, down to O-, and right to O, which bonds right to P. P double bonds up to O, bonds down to O-, and right to O, which bonds right to CH2. This bond line has a red arrow pointing back to its O. CH2 has a carbon chain on the right with 11 carbons. The second, sixth, and tenth carbons are double bonded and bond up. This carbon chain is labeled as farnesyl pyrophosphate. Below this is Ras in a blue oval, which bonds right to SH, which is labeled as Ras protein. The S has two red dots above with a red arrow pointing up to CH2. Below this is a down arrow representing farnesyl transferase (blue). To the right is an arrowing jutting to PPi. Below this is the Ras oval bonding right to S (pink), which bonds right to CH2 with the same carbon chain. This is all labeled as farnesylated Ras protein.
